## Summary

Deferred from #851 by operator instruction: create one v0.92.2 issue and stop current implementation. Complete actual executable proof and bounded Runtime repairs for five historical acceptance rows: RUST-01-ac-4, DRT-B-ac-2/ac-3, DRT-C-ac-2/ac-3. Parent disposition context: #522; review consumer: #833.

## Confirmed defect

Canonical Runtime ingress emits a correlated completion event on success but emits no corresponding failure event when dispatch returns an error. Failed work therefore lacks the Runtime-owned event needed to join authenticated Observatory failure responses and redaction evidence. A partial unreviewed fix adds a fixed, correlated `DomainWorkFailed` event; it is not delivered or proven.

## Remaining actual work

- Execute six distinct resident tick/ACC/UTS workloads through production code; retain real per-resident receipts and observable effects. Exercise production signed dehydration/restore and verify exact population/lineage, resumed work, tamper, omission and substitution rejection. Explicitly distinguish local mock provider from live model qualification.
- Exercise real provider subprocess failure, timeout/interruption and recovery with a healthy configured provider condition. Do not substitute caller-set failure flags or reference-trace labels for actual execution.
- Complete and test Runtime-owned failure event emission and authenticated WSS response/event correlation, redaction, and rejection of forged or mismatched evidence.
- Obtain immutable before/after Cargo-registered validation inventories for refactor baseline a71d699d52831b32bb68ed9c7c7e837925949de4 and merge e986de6d06aacd385de93dd033def77a718c1581. Source declarations are 50 to54; this is not an executed denominator or a reduction claim.
- Repair criterion-specific evidence validation and consumer inputs: bind exact criterion text/digest, source and producer revisions, actual execution/logs, complete scenario coverage and independent review. Reject synthetic metadata, stale revisions, absent review and cross-criterion substitutions.

## Existing evidence limits

#268 Run72 is real historical six-resident execution at8947231b6549f6b43f76c5d4656b333868a032ae; its producer hashes match, but detailed workload/population/restore receipts are privately retained and not in the public packet. #341 provider trace is explicitly local-reference-only and rejects supplied flags before provider invocation. #602 retains a reviewed exact-candidate Wuji live summary, not full event/response evidence; observability_not_ready remains explicit. Existing 41 focused component/fixture tests pass, but do not close these complete operational claims.

## Preserved partial work

Branch codex/851-reconcile-five-proof-links, base9c7e57d412d61898bd44ab00d53e31afbb779e5c. Uncommitted work remains in its registered FastWork worktree; no PR or merge is claimed.

- Kernel: src/telemetry.rs, src/ingress.rs, src/conversation_sessions_tests.rs, tests/governed_operations.rs. Provider build succeeded but wrong exact filter ran0tests; WSS additions remain unvalidated.
- ADL: src/long_lived_agent/tests.rs and tests/issue851_resident_proof.rs. Uncompiled; unfinished include_bytes path must be corrected before compilation; tamper proof/evidence manifest unfinished.
- Five-row packet and integrity verifier under docs/milestones/v0.92.1/evidence/release/tail-06/issue-851; incomplete, not accepted as proof.

## Validation starting points

`cargo test --locked --manifest-path adl-runtime-kernel/Cargo.toml --test governed_operations parity_c_live_governance::real_provider_process_loss_timeout_and_recovery_are_classified -- --exact`

`cargo test --locked --manifest-path adl-runtime-kernel/Cargo.toml --lib resident_agent_conversation_uses_canonical_agent_runtime_wss_ingress`

## Acceptance criteria

1. The Runtime failure-event defect is independently reviewed and covered by actual dispatch/WSS/redaction regressions.
2. All five rows have exact executable evidence; any genuine unsupported scope is explicitly owned and never silently promoted.
3. Registered before/after validation inventories are measured without facade or lexical-count substitution.
4. Negative cases reject synthetic, self-authored, stale, cross-criterion, missing-review and partial-scenario evidence.
5. #522/#833 consume the reviewed five-row result, preserving the separate five cloud-control and two execution-proof gaps and original19-finding denominator.
6. Focused proof and required CI pass at independently reviewed exact HEAD before publication.

## Non-goals

No paid cloud/GPU mutation, broad Runtime refactor, release approval, or automatic closure of #522/#833. Keep these five rows consolidated in this issue. Preserve historical evidence and do not claim partial uncompiled changes as delivery.

855.body:
## Summary

Make Runtime v3 dynamic agent admission provider-neutral. `csmctl agent add --config <agent.yaml>` currently accepts a generic provider field, but the Runtime admission and conversation paths hard-code a narrow provider allowlist and defer or reject otherwise valid registered providers.

## Goal

Allow an operator to add, inspect, communicate with, checkpoint, migrate, rehydrate, and remove an agent backed by any provider adapter registered with the Runtime, without restarting the Runtime or editing its canonical initialization file.

## Required Outcome

Dynamic agent lifecycle operations dispatch through the Runtime's provider registry and capability contract rather than provider-name match statements. Provider-specific authentication, endpoint validation, request execution, tool capability, streaming, accounting, and failure classification remain owned by the selected provider adapter.

## Deliverables

- Provider-neutral dynamic admission and conversation dispatch through the canonical provider registry.
- A provider capability contract covering conversation, tools, streaming, agent-to-agent communication, credentials, and model discovery or validation.
- Secure credential references in agent configuration; secret values never appear in agent YAML, API responses, logs, checkpoints, or lifecycle evidence.
- `csmctl` lifecycle support for dynamically admitted agents regardless of backing provider.
- Truthful roster/API/Observatory projection of provider, model, endpoint class, capabilities, health, and readiness.
- Focused fixtures and integration tests for local and hosted providers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `csmctl agent add --config <agent.yaml>` accepts every provider registered with the running Runtime and rejects only an unknown provider or a provider whose declared capability requirements are unsatisfied.
- Adding or replacing a dynamic agent does not require a Runtime or Guardian restart and does not require editing the Runtime initialization file.
- OpenAI/ChatGPT, Anthropic/Claude, Gemini through the appropriate Google provider route, Ollama local, and an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint each pass add, generated conversation, roster projection, checkpoint, removal, and rehydration tests.
- Agent-to-agent communication uses the same provider-neutral execution path and canonical agent names for every admitted provider.
- Provider adapters declare whether tools, streaming, model discovery, token accounting, and health checks are supported; the Runtime does not infer these capabilities from provider names.
- Hosted providers require HTTPS and approved credential references. Local plaintext endpoints remain limited to loopback, private, or explicitly trusted local-network bindings.
- Admission performs no recurring paid inference. Health checks and model validation follow provider capabilities and the metered-call safeguards tracked by #854.
- Provider failures retain actionable classifications such as credentials, quota, unsupported capability, model unavailable, transport, timeout, and invalid response.
- The API and Observatory report the effective provider/model and current capability/readiness state without exposing credentials.
- Deterministic tests prove that a newly registered fixture provider works without modifying Runtime admission or conversation match statements.

## Repo Inputs

- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/control.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/config.rs`
- `adl/src/cli/csmctl_cmd.rs`
- Existing provider adapter and capability architecture
- `docs/architecture/PROVIDER_CAPABILITY_AND_TRANSPORT_ARCHITECTURE.md`
- Issue #602 dynamic agent lifecycle behavior
- Issue #854 metered cloud inference safeguards

## Dependencies

- Coordinate with #854 so provider validation does not reintroduce periodic metered inference.
- Reuse existing provider adapters and credential-source contracts rather than duplicating provider clients inside Runtime control code.

## Demo Expectations

- On a running Runtime, add one local agent and hosted agents backed by OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini using `csmctl`, exchange operator and agent-to-agent messages, inspect their roster/API metadata, checkpoint them, remove them, and rehydrate them without restarting Runtime.

## Non-goals

- Hard-coding only the four providers used by the initial acceptance demonstration.
- Embedding provider secrets in agent configuration.
- Requiring all providers to support identical optional capabilities.
- Restarting Runtime merely to add, replace, or remove an agent.
- Changing subscription or cloud billing configuration.

## Issue-Graph Notes

- Target v0.92.2.
- Complements #854: #854 stops wasteful metered probes; this issue makes dynamic agents use any registered provider safely.

## Notes

The current implementation accepts `ollama`, `openai-compatible`, and `vertex_ai` at portions of validation, but live dynamic verification and conversation execution are narrower and Vertex live calls are deferred. Provider registration must become the authority instead of parallel string allowlists.

## Tooling Notes

- Use native C-SDLC v3 lifecycle commands.
- Stop after issue creation and bootstrap preparation; do not start implementation as part of issue creation.

862.body:
## Outcome

Decompose the oversized C-SDLC v3 local and remote command modules into cohesive, behavior-preserving components with thin module entrypoints.

## Problem

`csdlc-v3/src/commands/remote/mod.rs` is approximately 3,252 lines and combines GitHub issue and PR operations, authority validation, credentials, mutation intents, receipts, reconciliation, publication, and readback validation. `csdlc-v3/src/commands/local/mod.rs` is approximately 3,140 lines and combines binding, editing, validation, registrations, transactions, and local state persistence. Ordinary changes and reviews repeatedly require reading unrelated control-plane code, increasing review cost and regression risk.

## Deliverables

- Split remote command responsibilities into cohesive internal modules for authority, credentials, GitHub issue operations, GitHub PR operations, publication/readback, mutation reconciliation, receipts, and validation.
- Split local command responsibilities into cohesive internal modules for binding, editing, validation, registry/registration handling, transactions, and state persistence.
- Reduce both `mod.rs` files to clear module wiring and stable public dispatch interfaces.
- Preserve the existing public CLI, request/receipt schemas, durable paths, authority checks, operation digests, error codes, idempotency, and fail-closed behavior.
- Add or retain focused regression coverage at each extracted boundary.
- Record a before/after responsibility and source-size inventory so the change proves decomposition rather than moving complexity into another monolith.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Each extracted module owns one named responsibility with no circular dependency between command domains.
- [ ] `remote/mod.rs` and `local/mod.rs` are thin dispatch/module surfaces rather than implementation containers.
- [ ] Public APIs, serialized schemas, operation digests, stable error codes, CLI behavior, and persistent artifacts remain compatible.
- [ ] Existing native v3 command, authority, mutation, reconciliation, terminal, and negative-path tests pass unchanged or with relocation-only updates.
- [ ] New boundary tests cover accidental cross-route use and behavior-sensitive extraction seams.
- [ ] The before/after inventory shows where every moved responsibility landed and detects creation of replacement god modules.

## Non-goals

- Adding lifecycle features.
- Weakening authority, exact-head, topology, credential, or reconciliation guards.
- Redesigning schemas or changing user-visible behavior.
- Combining unrelated cleanup or product work with the structural refactor.

## Validation

- Native v3 focused unit and integration suites.
- CLI command-manifest and schema compatibility checks.
- Exact golden tests for operation digests, receipts, error codes, and durable paths.
- Module dependency/cycle check, responsibility inventory validation, and `git diff --check`.


<!-- csdlc-v3-operation:e0f3f1f7f4d31c0dc950c97d5fa00ed4c2c563ac281d673f48419c1108d3924f -->
862.title: [v0.92.2][C-SDLC v3][refactor] Decompose local and remote command god modules
